title: Hawkish Fed Repricing Returns as Rate-Hike Odds and Treasury Yields Climb to Multi-Month Highs
content: The Fed narrative flipped decisively hawkish across the window. Early in July new Chair Kevin Warsh branded inflation too high while stripping out forward guidance in favour of pure data dependence, and a benign June CPI briefly cooled hike bets and nudged USTs lower mid-month. That reprieve proved short-lived: with PCE running near 4.1% and a fresh energy shock lifting inflation expectations, futures swung from under 10% to roughly 35-50% odds of a quarter-point hike at the 29 July meeting. The repricing rippled across assets, with the two-year yield reaching about 4.37%, its highest since early 2025, the ten-year pushing above 4.7% and the thirty-year nearing 5.1%, tightening financial conditions and pressuring rate-sensitive equities. With Warsh silent on timing but adamant on inflation, every print now carries outsized weight for rates, FX and valuations.

title: Oil Vaults Back Above $100 as Middle East Escalation Threatens Hormuz and Red Sea Shipping
content: A renewed energy shock dominated commodities and fed the broader inflation debate as the Iran-US conflict intensified through the window. Brent crude vaulted back above $100 a barrel, its first close there since late May, gaining roughly 7% in a five-day surge after Yemen's Houthis struck Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea and Iran's Revolutionary Guard declared the Strait of Hormuz effectively closed. Iran's rejection of a US ceasefire offer deepened fears that Gulf supply could be throttled indefinitely, with Goldman Sachs flagging scope for Brent above $120 in the fourth quarter should Hormuz stay disrupted. The move reverberated widely, lifting energy shares, weighing on equity indices via margin and inflation worries, and reinforcing the hawkish rates narrative. Geopolitics reasserted itself as the key swing factor for inflation, growth and central-bank policy alike.

title: AI Capex Scepticism Weighs on Big Tech Even as Q2 Earnings Beat Broadly
content: The market's mega-cap engine faced fresh scrutiny as second-quarter earnings landed. Results were broadly strong, with the vast majority of S&P 500 reporters topping EPS estimates and profit growth holding up, yet investors fixated on the scale of artificial-intelligence spending rather than headline beats. Alphabet's numbers, and guidance for heavier capital expenditure, crystallised concerns that hyperscaler AI investment is outrunning near-term returns, sending the Nasdaq down more than 2% on 23 July and dragging the S&P 500 back towards 7,400. The episode extended a run of AI-led volatility from earlier windows, with leadership and index concentration again in focus as a handful of names drive benchmark direction. Combined with rising yields and dearer oil, the reassessment of AI economics left richly valued technology particularly exposed, keeping breadth, positioning and capex discipline central to the equity tape.
